newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close slightly up in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close slightly up in slow trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher after a listless Wednesday session and brokers expected the market to continue slow on a lack of fresh news.
The weighted index moved in a 33-point range and finished 24.23 points or 0.39 percent higher at 6,256.76. Turnover was a small T$35.9 billion.

The plastics sector outperformed the market to rise 1.8 percent in a rebound from low levels hit during recent market consolidation, brokers said. USI Far East gained 70 cents to T$29.7, Formosa Chemical Fibre was up 80 cents at T$32.6 and Formosa Plastics rose T$2 to T$58.

Hopes for an influx of foreign funds ahead of Morgan Stanley's planned September 2 inclusion of the Taiwan index in its global indices helped buying slightly, but sentiment was sluggish during the whole session.
The construction sector was hit by profit-taking on recent gains over an industry recovery, but brokers said the sector could rise again on expectations of further recovery.
Further substantial gains would require greater turnover, brokers noted. "Sentiment is not bad but the turnover is not enough to push up share prices," said Mike Tsai of Grand Cathay Securities.
Wang Jieh of Foremost Investment said many investors were sidelined awaiting fresh market-moving factors to emerge.
"The market could be pretty dull in the near term if there is no major news to inspire sentiment," Wang said.
Brokers saw resistance above 6,300 points while initial support was seen at 6,230 points.
